comparisons.reason: Both are any-comment binary features over OC_comments with the same 0/empty/null handling, but the constructs differ. Left requires a specific, identifiable real-world instance (event, person, case, place, study, etc.) used as support, and excludes generic or vague references. Right counts any external evidence, including statistics, empirical data, generic sources/links and documented facts. A comment citing general statistics or a link without a particular named instance counts for right but not left. Right also requires the evidence to support a counter-argument and come from outside the OP's post, which left does not state. Right is materially broader.
